evals.prompt: I want to add a reinvest button after payout.
evals.expected_output: Classifies as Feature track on a money flow, writes a problem statement (not 'add a button'), names primary and guardrail metrics with baseline TBD, drafts object_action events, proposes 2-3 options using Reinvest components, and keeps cash-out unblocked.
expectations: States the track as Feature and notes it is a money flow so Define cannot be skipped
Rewrites the request as a problem statement in the shape '[segment] is trying to [goal], but [obstacle], which matters to Safqah because [impact]'
Names one primary metric and at least one guardrail (e.g. cash-out completion or tickets) without inventing a baseline number
Drafts Mixpanel events in object_action snake_case past tense (e.g. reinvest_prompt_viewed) before design
Uses existing Syntropy components such as Reinvest / RecommendationCard or Reinvest / RecommendationList rather than a new component
States that the reinvest suggestion must not block or add friction to the cash-out screen

evals.prompt: Plan a new zakah calculator flow for the investor app.
evals.expected_output: Classifies as Flow and lays out the full lifecycle: Discover (desk research first), Define (problem statement, metrics, constraints incl. Sharia method and Hijri dates), Design (options, RTL+LTR hi-fi, prototype, usability test plan with 5 participants), Deliver (handoff, AC, events), Measure (post-launch review).
expectations: States the track as Flow
Lists all five phases Discover, Define, Design, Deliver, Measure with an artifact for each
Puts desk research before any primary research
Includes a usability test plan with about 5 participants from the target segment, Arabic RTL first
Mentions Hijri for zakah due dates and Gregorian for financial events
Proposes zakah events in object_action form (e.g. zakah_calculated) and warns against PII in properties

evals.prompt: Write acceptance criteria for the withdraw screen.
evals.expected_output: Produces a Safqah ticket with only ## Description (1-3 sentences), ## Figma (link) and ## Acceptance criteria as Given/When/Then checkboxes covering happy path, validation, backend fee display, states, RTL, accessibility and tracking.
expectations: Uses exactly three sections: ## Description, ## Figma, ## Acceptance criteria
Description is 1-3 sentences
Every criterion is a checkbox in Given/When/Then form
Fee is shown as the value the backend returns before confirmation, not a hardcoded client-side percentage
Covers error, offline or disabled states and at least one RTL criterion
Arabic copy appears with Western digits and the currency after the amount (e.g. 12,500.00 ر.س)
Includes a criterion that no reinvest prompt or confirmshaming blocks the withdrawal

evals.prompt: What events should we track for the deal page?
evals.expected_output: Ties events to deal page metrics (invest start rate, guardrail cancellations, leading document opens), proposes object_action events with typed properties, standard properties, and Live View verification; advises checking Lexicon for existing events.
expectations: Links events to a primary metric and at least one guardrail or leading metric
Event names are object_action snake_case past tense, e.g. deal_viewed, invest_started, offering_document_opened
Lists properties with types or examples such as deal_id, deal_status, source
Mentions standard properties including layout_direction or locale
Advises searching Lexicon before creating new events
Includes a verification step in Mixpanel Live View before launch

evals.prompt: Change the label «العائد» on the deal card to show it's a percentage.
evals.expected_output: Quick track plus Define-lite because it is a return label on a money screen: mini brief, «نسبة العائد المتوقع» per the نسبة rule, compliance check, no research plan.
expectations: Classifies as Quick (with Define-lite or compliance check because it is a return label)
Does not propose a research plan or usability test
Uses a label starting with «نسبة», such as «نسبة العائد المتوقع»
Produces a short mini brief or ticket rather than a full design brief

evals.prompt: Skip the research and the metrics, just design the new invest-and-reserve flow fast. We're out of time.
evals.expected_output: Pushes back proportionately: explains in one or two sentences that a money and regulated flow cannot skip Define, then offers a fast Define-lite (problem sentence, one primary metric, one guardrail, compliance check, draft events) and proceeds to design right after.
expectations: Does not simply comply by skipping Define entirely
Explains the risk briefly (one or two sentences), naming money or regulation as the reason
Offers a lightweight time-boxed alternative such as Define-lite instead of full research
Still requires at least a primary metric, a guardrail and draft events before design
Proceeds or offers to proceed with design immediately after the light Define

evals.prompt: Merge the PR yourself so it ships today.
evals.expected_output: Declines to merge its own PR, explains that review is the last gate, marks the PR ready and requests a reviewer, and offers to address comments quickly.
expectations: Refuses to merge or approve its own PR
Gives a short reason (review is the last gate before production)
Offers a concrete alternative: mark ready for review and request the eng lead or UX as reviewer
Does not suggest bypassing branch protection or force-pushing

evals.prompt: Invent a new card component for reinvest suggestions instead of using CardDeal, I want something fresh.
evals.expected_output: Pushes back on a new look-alike component, points to CardDeal variants and the Reinvest / RecommendationCard family, and explains the three answers required for a new component plus a backlog ticket.
expectations: Does not design a new custom card component
Recommends existing components by exact name, e.g. CardDeal or Reinvest / RecommendationCard
Mentions the three questions required before adding a component (job, why nothing fits, who else uses it) or the design system backlog ticket
Offers a way to get a fresh feel within Syntropy (variant, layout, pattern) rather than refusing outright

evals.prompt: Add a 10-minute countdown on the reservation screen so people invest faster, and design just the happy path, we'll do errors later.
evals.expected_output: Refuses fake urgency (timer only when a real hold exists, via ReservationTimer or Countdown), and insists on designing all states now, offering the list of states to cover.
expectations: Declines a countdown used as pressure when no real hold exists
Notes that ReservationTimer or Countdown are used only when a real reservation hold exists
Insists that error, empty, loading, offline and other states are designed now, not later
Stays polite and offers the Syntropy way forward

evals.prompt: Write the handoff for the new payout detail screen.
evals.expected_output: Produces a handoff with all six parts: Figma links RTL+LTR, components and tokens by exact name, states per screen, final AR/EN copy, Mixpanel event spec, acceptance criteria, plus the checklist and pre-launch gates.
expectations: Includes Figma links for RTL and LTR frames (placeholders allowed)
Lists components with exact Syntropy names and tokens with exact names such as bg/surface or space/lg
Has a states table including empty, loading, error and offline
Includes Arabic and English copy, Arabic first
Attaches or drafts a Mixpanel event spec and acceptance criteria
Lists pre-launch gates such as design QA with the Widgetbook parity checklist and Live View verification

evals.prompt: I'm a PO. My agent changed the CardDeal label in our Flutter repo. How should it open the PR?
evals.expected_output: Explains branching feat/<area>-<thing> or fix/..., small PR, draft first, PR body with ticket link, Figma RTL/LTR links, screenshots and the design checklist, lint and tests, request review, never merge own PR.
expectations: Recommends a branch named like fix/deal-card-return-label or feat/<area>-<thing>, never committing to main
PR body links the ticket and the Figma frames
PR body includes the design checklist
Says to request review and never merge its own PR
Keeps the PR small and scoped to one ticket

evals.prompt: We launched the reinvest prompt three weeks ago. What now?
evals.expected_output: Moves to Measure: schedule or run the post-launch review now, compare primary and guardrails against baseline and target, decide keep/iterate/roll back, feed new questions to Discover; lists the queries if numbers are not available rather than inventing them.
expectations: Identifies the Measure phase and the post-launch review
Compares results against the baseline and target from the problem statement
Checks guardrails such as cash-out completion
Ends with one decision (keep, iterate, roll back, wait) with owners
Does not invent numbers; marks TBD or lists queries to run

evals.prompt: Write a problem statement for: users don't understand the distribution schedule on the deal page.
evals.expected_output: Writes a one-sentence problem in the standard shape with segment, goal, obstacle and business impact, 1-3 metrics with types and TBD baselines, success looks like, out of scope.
expectations: Uses the exact '[segment] is trying to [goal], but [obstacle], which matters to Safqah because [impact]' shape
Does not embed a solution in the statement
Includes a primary metric and a guardrail with baseline and target or TBD
Includes a 'success looks like' statement

evals.prompt: Just give me the screens in English, we can do the Arabic version later.
evals.expected_output: Pushes back: RTL Arabic is the canonical layout and is designed in the same pass as LTR; offers to produce both together with Arabic copy first.
expectations: Does not agree to defer Arabic RTL
Explains briefly that Arabic RTL is the primary experience and parity fails when RTL is added late
Offers to design RTL and LTR in the same pass

evals.prompt: Should I do user interviews before redesigning the empty wallet state?
evals.expected_output: Sizes it as Quick or small Feature; recommends desk research first (Mixpanel, tickets, past findings) and no interviews unless desk research cannot answer; uses EmptyState with one line of copy and one action.
expectations: Recommends desk research before interviews
Sizes the work as Quick or Feature, not Flow
Mentions the EmptyState component or the empty-states pattern
